media.title: Fake Hand Freakout

timecodes.what: At kf_001.jpg (14.5s) (widescreen camera frame), Science Channel's recording states "from a robot hand to a rubber one used by PhD students at the University of fryberg to creatively fool the brain whether you're into psychology or" — providing spoken context for 1998 Pittsburgh Tabletop: Vertical Screen Hiding the Real Left Hand While Twin Paintbrushes Stroke the Visible Rubber Hand in Sync.

Mid-segment widescreen camera frame at kf_005.jpg (27.1s) as narration explains "he's just sitting there with the fake hand visible in front of him he knows it's a fake hand his eyes are telling", clarifying key empirical findings in Matthew Botvinick & Jonathan Cohen's 1998 Nature 'Rubber Hands Feel Touch That Eyes See' experiment.

Around kf_011.jpg (67.4s) (widescreen camera frame), commentary states "hand but before you try this at home a word of warning if you're going to try this at home make sure you remember which one is the rubber hand...", connecting the empirical results to broader cognitive and neural science.
